newsitem.title: ISRAEL: EU envoy says no deadline for Egypt mediation.
newsitem.headline: EU envoy says no deadline for Egypt mediation.

text.p: The European Union's Middle East envoy denied on Tuesday he had set a deadline for Egyptian efforts to solve the peacemaking crisis between Israel and the Palestinians.
Envoy Miguel Angel Moratinos issued the denial after Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak on Monday slammed his reported comments.
"I'm fully sorry that my declaration ... was misunderstood," Moratinos told Reuters.

"The European Union has never put a deadline to the excellent efforts of Egyptian diplomacy ... What I said was if in a certain time there is no way out we are willing to evaluate with Egypt and take more decisions."

On Monday, Mubarak, asked about a report that the European Union and the United States had agreed to give Egypt two more weeks to revive negotiations between Israel and the Palestinians, said: "The European envoy has no right to give Egypt a deadline to make progress in the peace process.
"We don't work for him and I'd like to give him a year or two to see how clever he is," Mubarak told reporters.

Israeli Radio on Sunday quoted Moratinos as saying that if Egypt's efforts failed within the two weeks then the United States, in conjunction with the European Union, would engage in "comprehensive crisis intervention".
Israeli and Palestinian negotiators met for the first time in more than two months in Cairo on Sunday under Egyptian auspices. There was no agreement but the sides said they would meet again.

After talks in Cairo last week, Moratinos and Egyptian Foreign Minister Amr Moussa gave different assessments of the chances of a breakthrough in the mediation to break an impasse over the building of a Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem.
Moratinos said he saw the beginnings of a solution to Israeli-Palestinian disputes and some openness on the part of Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.

But Moussa said: "It's far too early to be talking about openings especially after the statements made by Israel, and these are statements that are very damaging to any initiative and any action that can lead to an easing (in the situation)."

Moussa was reacting to a report that Netanyahu had spelled out for the first time his vision of a permanent peace settlement. Israel would keep key areas in the occupied West Bank, including Arab East Jerusalem, which is claimed by both Israel and the Palestinians.
